terms.meaning: A push or pull on an object, from its interaction with another object.
A force that acts against an object moving or trying to move over a surface.
The force with which the Earth attracts objects. It is always attractive.
The force exerted by a charged body on another body, charged or not.
The force with which the Earth pulls an object towards itself, measured in newtons.
The amount of matter in an object, measured in grams or kilograms.
The upward force from a liquid on an object in it.

items.name: Effects of a force
items.formula: It can change speed, direction of motion, or shape.
items.example: A kick changes a ball’s speed and direction. A press changes a clay ball’s shape.

items.name: Balanced forces
items.formula: Equal forces in opposite directions cause no change in motion.
items.example: In a tug-of-war with no winner, the rope stays still.

items.name: Force needs two objects
items.formula: A force comes from an interaction, and it stops when the interaction stops.
items.example: A hand pushes a door, and the door pushes back on the hand.

items.name: Contact forces
items.formula: Muscular force and friction need contact.
items.example: Lifting a bag uses muscular force.

items.name: Non-contact forces
items.formula: Magnetic, electrostatic and gravitational forces act at a distance.
items.example: A magnet pulls a pin before touching it.

items.name: What friction depends on
items.formula: The roughness of the two surfaces in contact.
items.example: A ball rolls farther on glass than on carpet.

items.name: Streamlined shapes
items.formula: Air and water also resist motion, so a pointed shape reduces this.
items.example: Aeroplanes, ships and high-speed trains are shaped this way.

items.name: Magnetic poles
items.formula: Like poles repel. Unlike poles attract.

items.name: Static charges
items.formula: Like charges repel. Unlike charges attract.
items.example: A balloon rubbed on hair picks up bits of paper.

items.name: Ball thrown upward
items.formula: It slows down, stops for an instant at the top, then speeds up as it falls.
items.example: Gravity pulls downward all the way.

items.name: Instruments
items.formula: Weight: spring balance. Mass: beam balance.
items.example: A spring balance is marked in newtons.

items.name: Weight on other worlds
items.formula: A mass of 1 kg weighs about 10 N on Earth and about 1.6 N on the Moon.
items.example: So 5 kg weighs about 50 N on Earth and 8 N on the Moon.

items.name: Archimedes’ principle
items.formula: Upthrust = Weight of the liquid displaced
items.example: An object that displaces 3 N of water feels 3 N of upthrust.

items.name: When an object floats
items.formula: The liquid it displaces weighs the same as the object. If less, it sinks.
items.example: A wooden block floats. A stone sinks.

items.name: Pumice stone
items.formula: This volcanic rock floats because it is full of air pockets.
items.example: It is one rock that does not sink.

mistakes.text: Weight and mass are different. Mass is the same everywhere, but weight changes from place to place.
Weight is measured in newtons, not kilograms. Kilograms are for mass.
Friction acts against the motion, not along with it.
A charged body can also attract an uncharged one, as with bits of paper.
